newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Rato reaffirms taxes to fall from 1999.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Rato reaffirms taxes to fall from 1999.

text.p: Spanish economy minister Rodrigo Rato reaffirmed on Tuesday that overall tax burden is to fall from 1999 as long as the public deficit is at two percent of gross domestic product (GDP), the EFE news agency reported.
Speaking at a university conference, Rato said this fall would guarantee more possibilities for workers to save.
This coincides with government forecasts for state revenues to fall as a percentage of GDP from 5.9 percent in 1998 to 5.7 percent in 1999 and 5.3 percent in the year 2000.

He added he expected April inflation to continue a declining tendency because in the period there were no new price pressures and the effect of a strengthening dollar had already been absorbed by the foreign exchange markets.
Inflation hit a 29-year low in March at 2.2 percent year on year.
